In gsm_titles, pull out duration and concentration in the title into two columns append
```{r}
# make df of the names of samples GSM, then for that column, apply function to get the title in metadata
gsm_titles <- data.frame(
  GSM = names(gsm_list),
  title = sapply(gsm_list, function(x) Meta(x)$title),
  chemical = sub("^chemical: ","",sapply(gsm_list, function(x) Meta(x)$characteristics_ch1[1])),
  duration = as.numeric(sub("^time point \\(days\\): ","",sapply(gsm_list, function(x) Meta(x)$characteristics_ch1[3]))), # days
  # duration_full = sapply(gsm_list, function(x) Meta(x)$characteristics_ch1[3]),
  dose = as.numeric(sub("^dose\\(um\\): ","",sapply(gsm_list, function(x) Meta(x)$characteristics_ch1[2]))), # (um)
  # dose_full = sapply(gsm_list, function(x) Meta(x)$characteristics_ch1[2]),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Meta(gsm_list[["GSM4295460"]])$title
```

Merge PFAS_metadata\$GEO_Accession..exp. file with gsm_titles\$GSM on the equivalent GSM#s --> reveal which SRR read belongs to which GSM on metadata file
```{r}
# rename PFAS_metadata\$GEO_Accession..exp. to PFAS_metadata\$GSM
PFAS_metadata <- PFAS_metadata %>% 
  rename('GSM' = 'GEO_Accession..exp.') %>%
  rownames_to_column('SRR') # rownames to be a column so don't disappear after merge


# put all df into list
df_GSMtoSRR <- list(PFAS_metadata, gsm_titles)

# merge all df in list
df_GSMtoSRR_merged <- df_GSMtoSRR %>% reduce(full_join, by='GSM')
```

To finish this task, we need to take the samples that are water
- then add them to markdups_counts_pfas_cleancols and raw_counts_pfas_cleancols
in the clean_data_PFAS.Rmd file

```{r}
markdups_ref_counts_water <- read.csv("./data/data_input_deseq/water_ref/markdups_counts_water.csv") %>% column_to_rownames("gene")
raw_ref_counts_water <- read.csv("./data/data_input_deseq/water_ref/raw_counts_water.csv") %>% column_to_rownames("gene")

# check that the row names are the same so that means genes are the same
# then combine the columns if true
if (identical(rownames(markdups_counts_pfas_cleancols), rownames(markdups_ref_counts_water))) {
  markdups_counts_pfas_cleancols <- cbind(markdups_counts_pfas_cleancols, markdups_ref_counts_water)
} else {
  stop("Row names do NOT match between markdups_counts_pfas_cleancols and markdups_ref_counts_water — check gene order/IDs before combining.")
}

if (identical(rownames(raw_counts_pfas_cleancols), rownames(raw_ref_counts_water))) {
  raw_counts_pfas_cleancols <- cbind(raw_counts_pfas_cleancols, raw_ref_counts_water)
} else {
  stop("Row names do NOT match between raw_counts_pfas_cleancols and raw_ref_counts_water — check gene order/IDs before combining.")
}
```

# Generating the files for Comparisons of Chemical v.s. Control
Knowing which SRR is which, means can filter out which samples in the count file belong to which

Files needed for DESeq for each comparison:
- counts file
- metadata file
*reorder the columns of featurecounts to be the same as rows in metadata*
*exact identical order

File to be outputted from HERE! :
- counts file with just the concerning samples

In the code to create DESeq, we will take that counts file and filter the metadata file to create the associated metadata file to process DESeq.


Compare between DMSO and PFOA (legacy)
- get the samples of concern in counts file

Make a function that can take in two chemicals to generate that counts file
```{r}
get_counts_comparison <- function(counts_file, control, chemical, time){
  
  # filter out rows for this specific control x chemical combination
  # goal is to get the associated SRR
  comparison_df <- GSMtoSRR %>% filter(chemical.y %in% c(control,chemical) & duration == time)
  
  # check if the control and the chemical is in comparison_df filtered from GSMtoSRR
  present <- c(control, chemical) %in% comparison_df$chemical.y
  print("check if the control and the chemical is in comparison_df filtered from GSMtoSRR")
  names(present) <- c(control, chemical)
  print(present)
  stopifnot(all(present))
  
  # Use the filtered SRR numbers to select only those SRR samples in counts file
  comparison_markdups_counts <- counts_file %>%
    select(comparison_df$SRR) # this would fail if SRR# not in counts_file
  
  # confirm that filtered counts file only contains those samples of the control x chemical combo
  cat(control," x ", chemical, " for ", time, " day/s\n", "File: ", deparse(substitute(counts_file)), "\n")
  cat("Successfully filter those SRR samples?\n",identical(comparison_df$SRR,colnames(comparison_markdups_counts)),"\n")
  cat("\n")
  
  return(comparison_markdups_counts)

  # return(list(hi=comparison_markdups_counts, hi2=comparison_df))
}
```

# Calling the function for each combination

## PFAS x Control
1 day, DMSO, PFAS:('PFOA','PFBS','PFOS','PFDS')
10 day, DMSO, PFAS
1 day, water, PFAS
10 day, water, PFAS
```{r}
output_dir <- "./data/data_input_deseq/PFASxControl"

#uncomment
# dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

durations <- c(1,10)
PFAS <- c('PFOA','PFBS','PFOS','PFDS')
controls <- c('DMSO', 'water') # figure out water after ref
counts_dfs <- list(markdups = markdups_counts_pfas_cleancols,
                   raw = raw_counts_pfas_cleancols)

for (duration in durations) {
  for (chemical in PFAS) {
    for (control in controls) {
      for (counts_name in names(counts_dfs)) {
        
        counts_df <- counts_dfs[[counts_name]]
        
        # this is if I want to save results as df in workspace
        # var_name <- paste0(chemical, "x", control, "_", duration, "_", counts_name)
        
        # assign(var_name, get_counts_comparison(counts_df, control, chemical, duration))
        # use assign so var_name is not replaced by results of get_counts_comparison()
        
        # get results
        result <- get_counts_comparison(counts_df, control, chemical, duration)
          
        # instead of save results as df, I save df as csv
        file_name <- paste0(chemical, "x", control, "_", duration, "_", counts_name, ".csv")
        
        #Uncomment
        # write.csv(tibble::rownames_to_column(result, "gene"),
                  file = file.path(output_dir, file_name),
                  row.names = FALSE)
      }
    }
  }
}
```
